newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LG Metals says Ok Tedi copper delayed.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LG Metals says Ok Tedi copper delayed.

text.p: LG Metals Corp, South Korea's largest copper smelter, said on Friday that a 10,000-tonne copper concentrate delivery from the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea had been delayed due to dry river conditions.

"We have been informed by Ok Tedi mine that about 10,000 tonnes of copper concentrates, which was set to arrive at a South Korean port by the end of July, will be delayed due to low water levels caused by the recent dry weather," Lee In-soo, manager of Public Affairs for LG Metals told Reuters.
He said the company did not anticipate any problems with copper production due to the delay as the volume of concentrate involved was not that large.
LG Metals consumes about 500,000 tonnes of copper concentrate a year, he added.
Ok Tedi is 52.6 percent owned by Australia's Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, with Canada's Inmet Mining Corp owning 17.4 percent and the rest held by the Papua New Guinea government.
LG Metals is an affiliate of South Korea's LG Group.
On Thursday, Japan's Nippon Mining and Metals Co said its June delivery of copper concentrate from Ok Tedi, estimated at about 25,000 tonnes, had also been delayed.
